title: Secure Code Warrior Research Finds Curated Security Rule Sets Cut Measured Risk in AI-Generated Code by Up to 70%
headline: Secure Code Warrior research highlights impact of security rules on AI-generated code
summary: Secure Code Warrior released findings from its AI Trust Index, which benchmarks the security of code generated by over 30 AI models. The research demonstrates that applying curated security rules can reduce vulnerabilities in AI-generated code by up to 70%. It also indicates that model performance varies significantly, with some budget models outperforming flagship models in security metrics.
why_it_matters: Organisations must implement structured governance, such as curated security rules and prompt engineering, rather than relying on default model settings to mitigate the inherent security risks of AI-assisted software development.

quotes.text: Vague instruction does little, while curated rules cut measured risk by up to 70%: The default model sets the starting point; the prompt decides how secure AI-generated code ends up.
Today’s models know approaches to secure coding, but they don’t do it by default. The harness, prompts and rules they’re given decide how secure the output is

classification.significance_reason: Provides empirical evidence for security controls in AI-assisted development, relevant for organisations managing software supply chain risk.
